# CG-REQ-013: Request body removed

The operation no longer documents a request body.

**Why it matters:** Consumer impact depends on how the provider handles unexpected bodies.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Area | [Requests](./#req) |
| Detects | `requestBody.removed` |
| Severity | breaking: high · potentially breaking: medium · undetermined: medium |
| Classification can be overridden | no (the rule only fires when the change is breaking by definition) |

## Message

> The request body of {operation} was removed.
>
> The provider may ignore or reject bodies; whatever the body controlled is lost.
>
> **Fix:** Confirm how the provider treats bodies that are still sent.

## Examples

Each example is an executed test case of the rule (`packages/engine/test/compat/fixtures.ts`).

### Fires: body removed

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
-   /x:
-     post:
-       requestBody: {content: {application/json: {schema: {type: object}}}}
-       responses: {'204': {description: ok}}
+   /x: {post: {responses: {'204': {description: ok}}}}
```

**Result:** Potentially breaking, medium. The request body of POST /x was removed.

### Does not fire: media type removed, body remains

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      post:
-       requestBody: {content: {text/plain: {}, application/json: {schema: {type: object}}}}
+       requestBody: {content: {application/json: {schema: {type: object}}}}
        responses: {'204': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** no finding from this rule.

## Limitations

- Provider handling of unexpected bodies is not described by OpenAPI.

## Silence or tune it

```yaml
rules:
  ignore:
    - rule: CG-REQ-013
      operation: "GET /example"   # optional: narrow it down
      reason: "Explain why this is acceptable"
      expires: 2027-01-01         # optional
  overrides:
    CG-REQ-013: { severity: low }
```
